That's higher than 276.0666 by 0.0332. Maybe formula C14H12O6: C14=168, H12=12.0939, O6=95.9695 total =276.0634. That's close to 276.0666 (difference 0.0032). So likely C14H12O6. The carbon NMR shows 14 carbons? Actually list has 14 deltas: 166.00,151.10,144.35,140.45,137.05,131.30,131.30,124.40,122.30,119.00,116.65,116.65,61.10,14.26. That's 14 distinct carbon signals, suggests 14 carbons. So formula C14H12O6 matches 14 carbons. Good.

Now need to deduce structure. Peaks: carbonyl carbons around 166 (likely ester or acid). 151-144 aromatic carbons. 61.10 (maybe O-CH2). 14.26 (methyl). So maybe a methyl ester attached to aromatic ring with multiple carbonyls (maybe a dimethoxy? Actually OCH2 at 61 suggests -O-CH2- maybe a methoxy? But methoxy carbon ~55. So 61 could be O-CH2 attached to carbonyl (e.g., -CH2-O-CO-). Methyl at 14.26 typical aliphatic CH3.

C14H12O6 suggests maybe a coumarin derivative? Coumarin (C9H6O2) plus extra groups.

Let's search isomers list for C14H12O6. The earlier list includes many candidates. Need one that matches NMR: aromatic carbons many, carbonyls, OCH2, methyl.

Another candidate: 'COC1=C2C(=C(C(=C1)C(=O)O)OC)C=CC=C2C(=O)O' maybe a dimethoxy benzoic acid? Contains methoxy (55) and carbonyl.

But we have a methyl at 14.26, suggests a CH3 attached to carbonyl (acetyl) maybe an acetate group (CH3-CO-O). Carbonyl carbon ~170, methyl ~20-30? Actually acetyl methyl ~30. 14 is more like aliphatic CH3 attached to sp3 carbon (e.g., -CH3 attached to aromatic? maybe a methyl on aromatic (toluene) gives ~20 ppm for carbon. 14 is typical for methyl attached to sp3 carbon (e.g., ethyl). Could be a methyl attached to carbonyl (acetate) gives ~20-30. 14 is low, maybe a methyl attached to O (methoxy) is ~55, not 14. So maybe a methyl on a saturated carbon (e.g., isopropyl). But only one methyl.

Also OCH2 at 61 suggests -CH2-O- maybe part of an ester side chain: -COOCH2-.

Thus maybe structure: methyl 2-(hydroxy)acetate attached to aromatic? Actually -O-CH2-CO- (glycolate) gives CH2 at ~60, carbonyl at ~170, methyl of acetate at ~20. But we have methyl at 14, not 20.

Could be -CH2-CH3 (ethyl) attached to O? Ethoxy carbon CH2 ~60, CH3 ~15. Yes ethoxy group: -O-CH2-CH3. That matches CH2 at 61, CH3 at 14. So we have an ethyl ester.

Thus molecule likely contains an ethyl ester (C2H5O-). So formula includes C2H5O (C2H5O). The rest aromatic with carbonyls.

C14H12O6 includes 6 oxygens. Ethyl ester contributes 2 O (C=O and O-CH2). Leaves 4 O elsewhere, maybe two more carbonyls (e.g., two carboxylic acids or esters) and maybe phenolic OH.

Thus candidate: Ethyl 2,4-dihydroxybenzoate? That would be C9? Not.
